title: runtime: add fast-path gating and safe-mode fallbacks for kernel precision/scheduling
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: We observed two operational classes of failures in the field: (1) numerical degradations when aggressive low-precision kernels (int8/quantized) are selected for edge cases, and (2) intermittent correctness regressions after kernel switchovers combined with continuous batching and KV-cache reuse. This PR introduces a coordinated fast-path gating and safe-mode fallback system: 1) a runtime fast_path_gating layer that only selects optimized kernels when a set of preconditions are satisfied (sequence length, cache state, numeric stability score), 2) precision toggles that make it possible to prefer bf16/fp16 over int8 for tensors flagged as high-sensitivity, 3) a safe-mode that dynamically falls back to reference kernels and conservative scheduling if numeric checks fail post-inference, and 4) scheduler integration so fallback decisions are propagated to batching and KV cache reuse policies. Changes are conservative and opt-in via the runtime config; the default remains high-performance but with improved detection and graceful fallback when anomalies are observed. The description below enumerates changes, test coverage, CI, benchmarks, and rollout plan.

review_comments: Michael Chen: Please add a micro-benchmark showing the cost of safe-mode triage on 8k request runs. We need numbers to justify the default config.

Asha Patel: Added bench_fallbacks.md with end-to-end numbers (see files_changed). Safe-mode checks add ~1-2% per-token overhead on our fp16 baseline for the checked codepaths; worst case with full validation is ~8%.
Riley Thompson: Why not do the KV cache validation lazily? We should avoid cross-request blocking.

Asha Patel: The first implementation used lazy validation but we observed cascading correctness issues. This change keeps validation in the hot-path but bounds the work (sampled checks + checksum) and has a scheduler-driven deferred full-validate option.
Sofia Alvarez: Please ensure this is opt-in for Dedicated/private customers via config; an accidental toggle flip could regress latency-sensitive workloads.

Asha Patel: Done. runtime config defaults to existing behavior; new flags are disabled unless explicitly flipped via config or rollout policy. Added docs section describing recommended rollout (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
Michael Chen: CI failing on a flaky integration test (test_streaming_consistency). Can we isolate?
Asha Patel: Fixed an ordering race in scheduler when fallback_signal arrives during an in-flight continuous batch. Added a deterministic unit test and retriggered CI.

release_notes: Introduce runtime fast-path gating and safe-mode fallbacks: opt-in precision toggles (fp16/bf16/int8), KV-cache validation hooks, and scheduler-aware fallback propagation. Improves production safety when using low-precision kernels at minor cost to hot-path latency when checks are enabled. Rollout recommended as canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with performance guardrails.
